body:
Global crypto markets logged a mixed session on September 25, 2026, with the total market cap sitting at $2.9T after a 24-hour decline of 0.93% even as most individual assets printed green. That apparent contradiction resolves quickly when you look at BTC dominance at 58.3% and ETH dominance at 11.4%: bitcoin is treading water while capital rotates aggressively into mid- and large-cap altcoins, compressing the headline market cap figure as some profit-taking bleeds into stablecoin positions. Total 24-hour volume came in at $110.9B, healthy enough to confirm that the altcoin moves are not purely thin-market noise. The Fear and Greed index held steady at 71 both today and yesterday, a reading of Greed that is not yet at the frothy extremes that historically precede sharp corrections, but a level that demands respect heading into the weekend.

BTC settled at $84,360, up 1.07% over 24 hours and a solid 8.17% on the week, though the 1-hour print of -0.12% tells you the last couple of hours have been directionless. The CoinDesk headline that bitcoin holders are cashing out but not in the way seen at prior tops is the nuance traders need here: distribution is happening, but the structure looks more like healthy rotation than the euphoric blow-off selling that marked 2021 and early 2024 peaks. On the ETF side, Bitcoin ETF inflows slowed to $191M in the latest session as a six-day streak reached a cumulative $2.8B according to Cointelegraph, and separately CoinDesk reports that Bitcoin ETFs have erased a $5.8B hole, meaning the institutional bid has been persistent and structural. The $84,000 level is the immediate floor to defend; a clean hold there keeps the weekly uptrend intact, while a break and retest of the low $82,000s would be the first real stress test for the bull case.

ETH at $2,709.44 matched BTC's weekly performance exactly at +8.17%, but outperformed on the 24-hour read with a gain of 2.46% on volume of $15.28B, suggesting some incremental preference for ETH over BTC at current prices. The real energy today was elsewhere in the altcoin complex. LINK was the standout, up 13.74% to $13.95 on volume of $1.01B, a move that warrants attention given Chainlink's sensitivity to oracle demand and cross-chain activity narratives. XRP surged 9.61% to $1.61, extending its 7-day gain to 19.71%, while AVAX's 7-day performance of +32.21% to $10.59 makes it the stealth winner of the week even if its 24-hour gain of 5.37% looks modest by today's standards. ADA at $0.255312 and UNI at $9.78 both cleared 8% on the day, the latter with a sharp 1-hour spike of 4.77% that bears watching for follow-through. BNB at $778.31 was the clear laggard, up only 0.99% over 24 hours and just 3.63% on the week, diverging noticeably from the rest of the complex.

The macro backdrop is quietly uncomfortable in a way that crypto is choosing to ignore for now. The CoinDesk headline on bond volatility surging while bitcoin and Wall Street stay calm is the key tension: fixed-income markets are pricing something disruptive that equity and crypto vol surfaces are not. That divergence has historically resolved in one direction, and it is rarely the bond market that blinks first. On the regulatory and legal front, KelpDAO has sued LayerZero and its CEO over what Cointelegraph describes as a $292M rsETH bridge exploit, characterized as the largest exploit of 2026 so far. Bridge security remains the sector's most persistent attack surface, and a lawsuit of this size will sharpen regulatory focus on cross-chain infrastructure at an already sensitive moment. The Samourai Wallet co-founder situation and the Magic Eden NFT security scare add further noise to the compliance and custody risk picture.

Heading into the next session, 3 things matter most. First, whether the Bitcoin ETF inflow streak extends beyond 6 days or stalls; a break in that streak would be the first tangible sign that institutional demand is softening at current prices. Second, the bond volatility signal deserves a specific catalyst watch: any surprise move in the long end of the Treasury curve or a hawkish Fed communication could reprice risk assets quickly given that crypto vol is priced cheaply relative to fixed income vol right now. Third, the LayerZero exploit lawsuit will generate headlines and could trigger contagion sentiment around interoperability protocols more broadly, so any names with heavy cross-chain bridge exposure should be on the risk-reduction watchlist. The bull case stays alive as long as $84,000 holds on BTC and altcoin volume remains above the thresholds seen today, but the combination of greed at 71, rotating distribution in BTC, and an unresolved macro tension in rates makes this a session for tighter stops rather than size-up aggression.
